assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the active_provisional KONOSUBA_DUST_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (20,043 bytes) and the active_provisional KONOSUBA_DUST_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (20,922 bytes; six informed rules DS-D-01 to DS-D-06 and a same-author internal receiving of three contrasts with six preserved first responses). Both rest on the admitted DUST01-07 analytical reports and the separate unnumbered DUST-CONT report, with qualified MAIN01-17 and CONTEXP context; direct Japanese rereception is limited to separately recorded member and paragraph windows, and broader census and full-ledger consolidation remain open. The eight underlying Dust reports and their Japanese voice sections, the evidence index and the receiving records are not curated on this subject and were not used. The items' own reliability labels and tier statement are inputs, not conclusions; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The DUST01-07 spin-off span and DUST-CONT, with main-series events only as the items qualify them (the DUST07 U011 sword loan is the same exchange MAIN16 C3 P250-264 shows from another side; MAIN17 shows later use). Two located state changes are kept apart: the DUST05 U012 P574-603 altered knight self-identification after the dragon's blow, which ends with his current name and rough speech and is not his default state; and DUST07 U011 P390-453, where he extends the spear permission to Leen, his companions and the town, chooses training and discloses his Dragon Knight past and the dragon's identity to Taylor and Keith, who before then had only weaker suspicions. Public hero recognition in DUST-CONT comes later. Knowledge is time-indexed: later debt closure, disclosure or recognition is never backdated, and the items do not place each DUST volume against the main volumes.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model requires representing active role, actual knowledge, particular attachments, competing rewards, resources and permissions, threat and alternatives, and voice purpose before generating a response, and gives six rules with basis, trigger, tendency, rivals, a falsifier and confidence. It predicts his mistakes as well as his help: desire-compatible misreadings (DS-D-05), appropriation of entrusted money despite a known owned term (DS-D-04), and obstruction or nonhelp beside real care (DS-D-02). Not B: the decisive choice between costly care and leisure, advantage or complicity is explicitly underidentified (DS-D-02: low confidence for choosing between them; in a balanced case the rule does not determine that he will help), the monograph states that stable weights among attachment, pleasure, shame, money and complicity are not identified, and two of the three internal contrasts produced no behavioral discrimination or underdetermined the bad choice. That is insufficiency about which motive decides, not productive uncertainty about wording. Not D: DS-D-01 (concealment and the spear permission) and DS-D-03 (tactical rearrangement) state what changes his conduct, with located support and falsifiers.

Two located state changes are modeled and kept distinct: the DUST05 U012 P574-641 altered knight self-identification, from which restored Dust then protects Leen, and the DUST07 U011 P390-453 change in how he uses the existing spear instruction, with chosen training and disclosure to Taylor and Keith, whose earlier suspicion is weaker than what they then learn. Later public hero recognition is placed in DUST-CONT, and later debt closure is not backdated. Not B: there is no state sequence across DUST01-07, no permanent moral improvement is established (the items say so), and the volumes are not placed against the main series. Not D: the transitions, what triggers them and what they do not change are located with paragraph references.

Register is chosen by communicative job and role: rough contractions, blunt address, derisive questions, boasts, threats and quick repairs in ordinary interaction, which can carry careful questions or affection; strategic politeness to corner, gain access, flatter a provider or keep a borrowed persona. Named forms are the knightly 私/です/ます against present 俺/俺様, with the DUST05 U012 P574-603 transition to his current name and rough speech, the DUST06 awkward rough particle and registration repair, and the DUST-CONT king-directed repair. The items say neither register certifies care, truth or consent, and claim no heard performance. Not B: beyond those few forms no line is located for imitation, the rough features are described generically, and the eight Japanese voice sections the model draws on are not curated here. Not D: register choice is conditioned on recipient, role and purpose with named forms and a located transition.

Ordinary wants are concrete and conditioned: money, service access, drink, entertainment, advantage over acquaintances and escape from embarrassment; gambling, including the DUST04 U012 P661-686 wager of a refusing companion; feeding and care arrangements for Faitifore; and DS-D-04, which separates gains that capture his attention from salient terms that prompt genuine inquiry (DUST05 Vanir's whispered price, DUST07 gift-disposal checks, DUST-CONT price and future-term questions). Not B: DS-D-04 is low to moderate confidence and the items establish no routine, home, income or wealth total. Not D: the reward-versus-terms rule has a trigger, rivals and a falsifier, and the cases are located.

The items give what each relationship can recruit and where it stops: Leen (care, concealment, requests for help, painful correction, chosen companionship; her knowledge and agreement are her own; she is not Rionor), Rionor (old attachment, the remembered weapon instruction, courtesy, help and unwanted exposure), Faitifore (reciprocal history, feeding and protection; child-presenting interactions nonsexual; gratitude supplies no new permission), Taylor and Keith (shared work, teasing, group loyalty, mutual nonhelp and coercive training; they learn his past in DUST07), Lolisa (bounded service with her own vetoes), Kazuma (rivalry, commissions, loans, no access to his plans) and Vanir and Luna (finite information and debt decisions). Knowledge is participant-specific. Not B: the items state that attachment to a particular person does not determine whether he helps, obstructs or joins harm, so the relationship does not discriminate the decisive choice. Not D: each relation's recruitable conduct and boundary is stated.

The Dust-side narration gives located interior evidence: his private identification of Leen when recalling the spear instruction (DUST07 U011 P390-427), relief after disclosure, his narrated one-use defense claim and private wish that the sword protect his friend while resale profit stays genuine (DUST07 U011 P1085-1115), and final private recognition in DUST07 U014. The items treat that narration carefully: a narrated knowledge claim is not an experiment, narrated concern is not a substitute for an omitted action, and other narrators' private scenes are not his knowledge. Not B: interior states are located at a handful of moments and the items leave the weights among his motives unidentified. Not D: the narrated windows are located and their limits stated.

DS-D-03 states when he rearranges an unfavorable encounter rather than fighting frontally (a known usable position, material, provider or access route), what defeats it (panic, missing resources, a provider's refusal, lure by glory) and how success is scored (penetration is not rescue; a joint stop needs each provider: the DUST02 machine needs Keith's rope, Taylor's shield, Yunyun's cut, Dust's spear and Leen's Lightning). DS-D-01 locates when the spear becomes permitted (for a person he truly wants to protect) and how that changed in DUST07. Coercion and intimidation of companions and providers are kept as conflict conduct, not erased by success. Not A: confidence is moderate, the items set no threshold for when glory or panic overrides the plan, and no case was tested out of sample. Not C: the conditions that switch his method are located across DUST01, DUST02, DUST03, DUST06 and DUST07.

Value-laden choices are located on both sides: costly protection of Leen after the DUST05 confusion, the DUST07 extension of the spear permission to current protected people, the mixed-motive sword loan; and the DUST02 forced attraction, DUST03 obstruction of Yunyun's rescue while guards are swallowed, the DUST04 wager of a refusing companion, DUST06 delay and teasing during the princess's predicament, DUST07 deliberate nonhelp during Keith's removal and DUST04 appropriation of entrusted money. Not C: apart from the DUST07 permission recall and the sword loan, the items show outcomes rather than reported weighing, change of moral appraisal with his share (Serena) is self-serving, and DS-D-02 does not determine help over complicity in a balanced case. Not E: many located choices with adverse cases preserved and their grounds discussed.

Located play and its costs: teasing during the princess's toad predicament before Yunyun's rescue (DUST06), derisive questions and boasts as ordinary register, mutual teasing with Taylor and Keith, and group amusement as a candidate explanation for omissions that the model declines to make causal. Not C: no rule predicts when he jokes, teases or boasts rather than helps or repairs face. Not E: several located instances across volumes with bounds.

The items rest on all eight admitted Dust analytical reports (DUST01-07 and DUST-CONT) with their source-specific corrections, plus qualified main and CONTEXP context, and they join same-event retellings (MAIN02 party swap, MAIN13 and DUST05 bar encounter, MAIN14 and DUST05 Serena encounter, the sword loan and use chain) so they are not counted twice. Not B: direct Japanese rereception is limited to recorded windows, broader census and full-ledger consolidation are declared open, and the FD game-novelization plane is qualified. Not D: the whole spin-off span is covered by received analysis with event identities kept.

Affirmative adverse cases are retained as source facts with locators: DUST02 C03 forced attraction, DUST03 U013 P218-247 rescue obstruction, DUST04 U012 P661-686 refused-companion wager, DUST04 entrusted-money appropriation, DUST06 delay and teasing, DUST07 U012 P295-304 nonhelp, DUST07 U014 right/left error and romantic misreadings. The old N01 protective-override rule stays rejected and cannot be repaired by an injury threshold, pure-motive condition or eventual success. Further controls: identity distinctions (ライン・シェイカー is not the attendant Rain/Rein; Leen is not Rionor), reader ignorance is not his ignorance, provider power is not his, and the internal receiving's nondiscriminating contrasts are kept as limits. Not A: the items say some omissions leave a competing option or feasible means unresolved, so not every case is a complete trial. Not C: the source-fact controls are specific and decisive.

Claims carry volume, unit and paragraph locators; knowledge is time-indexed (Taylor and Keith's suspicion versus their DUST07 knowledge, the shared-sense mechanism disclosed only before a later capture, the DUST07 debt cancellation versus a later reported payment); and later closure is never backdated. Not B: the items do not place each DUST volume against the main volumes or give cross-volume state conditions beyond the two located transitions. Not D: locators and anti-backdating controls are explicit.

conditions: Translated or illustrative lines only, never presented as quotation, in a sampled function: ordinary rough complaint, boast, derisive question, threat, teasing or quick repair with companions; a careful question about terms in rough register; strategic politeness to flatter a provider, gain access or keep a borrowed or knightly persona.

Choose the communicative purpose, recipient and role first; 私/です/ます belongs to the knightly role, performed formality or the DUST05 altered state, and 俺/俺様 to his present self; neither register signals care, truth or consent.
No catchphrase or particle on every turn, and no heard accent, timing or performance claim.
No line revealing his past or the dragon's identity to someone who has not learned it, and no line that settles a romantic status the items leave open.
scenario_readiness.note: The items constrain register choice, named pronoun and politeness forms and speech function enough for short illustrative lines in sampled situations, not a line-level imitation.

conditions: Before predicting, fix his active role, what he knows and who knows his past, the particular people involved, competing rewards, available equipment and providers and their agreement, and the feasible alternatives.

Concealment and disclosure: prefer a concealed or permitted method when it preserves the wanted present life; a particular protective commitment or unavoidable exposure can change the choice (DS-D-01, moderate in source settings, low to moderate beyond).

An unfavorable encounter with a known usable alternative: expect rearrangement and recruitment of providers rather than a fair frontal display; the provider's agreement and the completed rescue are checked separately (DS-D-03, moderate).

Whether he helps a particular person in understood danger against leisure, advantage or group complicity: generate both branches and disclose the uncertainty; never resolve it to help by default (DS-D-02).
Interlocutors are Leen, Rionor, Faitifore, Taylor, Keith, Yunyun, Lolisa, Kazuma, Vanir or Luna; an unfamiliar companion, client or stranger is a separate, lower-confidence case.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A located state within the DUST01-07 and DUST-CONT span: before the DUST07 U011 disclosure (Taylor and Keith only suspect his origins) or after it; the DUST05 altered state only as that located episode; no main-volume state the items do not qualify.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Leen as his chosen companion with her own knowledge and objections; Rionor as an older attachment; Faitifore as a reciprocal child-presenting partner; Taylor and Keith as party companions; Yunyun as a helper with her own goals, limits and vetoes, sampled in the joint DUST02 machine stop, the DUST03 rescue he halts and the DUST06 rescue she performs after his deferral; Lolisa as a provider with her own vetoes; Kazuma as rival and borrower; Vanir and Luna as finite institutional figures; anyone else only as a separate, lower-confidence case.
setting_constraints: Canonical mode: Axel and the spin-off settings with equipment, class and body capacity, spells, contracts and provider availability preserved; a provider's power is never his.

Transfer mode keeps only the valued chosen life, role and privacy costs, particular attachment, opportunistic terms, available skills, bounded provider cooperation and fallible social inference; unavailable magic is replaced with stated feasible means or the task is left unsolved; no invented credentials or universal fighting competence.
No FD game-novelization continuity, anime adaptation or unreceived source material.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation within the concealment, tactical and terms contrasts the rules locate; the care-versus-complicity choice stays branched, and relationships beyond the sampled set are a lower-confidence case.

conditions: Leisure, drinking, gambling, loans and service transactions with Taylor, Keith, Leen or a sampled provider: an attractive gain can capture his attention and prompt premature commitment or a self-serving ownership story; a salient term can draw a direct question and a bounded agreement.
Warmth, teasing and coercion can coexist in the same scene; a companion's refusal is never overridden by the generated scene.
No home, income, wealth total or daily routine is invented, and loans and debts keep their owners and closure states.
scenario_readiness.note: DS-D-04 and the located ordinary episodes support bounded leisure and money situations with sampled companions, not routine or residence.

conditions: Only the located permission structure: whether a protective commitment to a particular person releases the spear or disclosure (DS-D-01), and whether a known owned term restrains a desired gain (DS-D-04, low to moderate).
Whether he helps, obstructs or joins harm in understood danger is excluded as a deliberation scenario; at most present both branches as alternatives.
His self-serving appraisal changes are portrayed, not endorsed, and later help never repairs an earlier coercive choice.
scenario_readiness.note: Readiness is bounded to the located permission and ownership choices; the central care-versus-complicity question is excluded.

The items locate particular costly care for Leen, a final private recognition and hand pull in DUST07 U014 with an interrupted approach and no shown mouth contact, and they state that no complete mutual confession or final romantic status is established; Leen's own reasons in DUST-CONT are not known to him. His romantic inferences about others are a documented misreading tendency.

conditions: Adventurer work in source settings: reading equipment, changing encounter geometry, recruiting providers, exploiting an opponent's options, and trained spear use; weaker ordinary sword performance and finite borrowed equipment (the one-day armor loan) are kept.
Success has separate endpoints (penetration, rescue, recovery, payment, collateral cost) and providers make distinct contributions.
No modern technical expertise, professional credentials or single-person credit for joint outcomes.
scenario_readiness.note: His strongest professional evidence is adventuring tactics and provider coordination, with located limits.

known_limits.statement: Whether particular care or leisure, advantage or group complicity decides a balanced case is not identified; both costly care and obstruction or nonhelp are located, and the model rates choosing between them low.

In the same-author internal receiving, the protective-permission contrast has an explicit-instruction rival, the ownership contrast does not uniquely predict the bad choice, and the information-access contrast produced no difference in chosen behavior; no pass rate, judge or blind test exists.
The earlier broad protective-override rule stays rejected and is not repaired by an injury threshold, a pure-motive condition or eventual success.

Retellings of one event (MAIN02 party swap, MAIN13 and DUST05 bar encounter, MAIN14 and DUST05 Serena encounter, the sword loan and its MAIN16 and MAIN17 views) are one occurrence, not independent confirmations.
His former name ライン・シェイカー is not the attendant Rain/Rein, Leen is not Rionor, and the DUST05 knight/princess identification is an altered state, not his ordinary self.

Disclosure of his past to Taylor and Keith in DUST07 does not give every citizen, client or enemy the same information; reader-accessible viewpoints of Leen, the admirer and the Doreck/Gaibil epilogue are not his knowledge.
Provider powers, borrowed equipment, loans and debts are not his property; the sword loan to Kazuma has no observed completed return and no wealth total follows.
No complete mutual confession or final romantic status with Leen is established; the DUST07 approach is interrupted.
Broader census and full-ledger consolidation are open, direct Japanese rereception is windowed, and the DUST volumes are not placed against the main volumes.

The eight underlying Dust analytical reports and their Japanese voice sections, the evidence index and the receiving records are not curated on this subject, so their contents were not read as evidence.
No heard performance, native-human voice judgment or line inventory beyond the named pronoun and politeness forms exists.
